text:
I just finished "How Big Things Get Done" by Bent Flyvbjerg and Dan Gardner. Every planner should read it.

One set of numbers stayed with me. Out of 16,000 projects:
• fewer than half finished on budget
• 8.5 % finished on budget and on time
• 0.5 % finished on budget, on time and with the promised benefits

That is 1 project in 200.

Five lessons I am taking to site:

1. Think slow, act fast. Planning is cheap. Delay on site is expensive. Plan until the questions are answered, then build without stopping.
2. Start with why. Know what the project is for before the first drawing.
3. Your project is not unique. Look at how similar projects really went, not at how you hope yours will go.
4. Build with Lego. Small things repeated many times get faster and better. One big custom thing does not.
5. Your biggest risk is you. Optimism, pressure to start early, and "we will fix it later".

On most projects I have seen, we do the opposite. We plan fast and build slow.

Which of these five does your project break most often?
